name: businessbench_v1
description: BusinessBench v1 is a 17-question benchmark testing practical business mathematics: pricing and markup, discounts, payroll and overtime, profit margins, break-even analysis, simple and compound interest, ROI, commissions, sales tax, inventory turnover, depreciation, percentage change, and conceptual reasoning about pricing and revenue. Questions are self-contained word problems with unambiguously computable answers, mixing numeric, exact, contains, and list answer types.

questions.question: A retailer buys an item for $40 and applies a 25% markup on cost. What is the selling price in dollars?
A jacket is priced at $120 and is on sale at 15% off. What is the sale price in dollars?
An employee earns $18 per hour. In one week they work 42 hours, with all hours beyond 40 paid at 1.5x. What is their gross pay for the week in dollars?
A company has revenue of $85,000 and total costs of $59,500. What is its profit margin as a percentage?
A business has fixed costs of $12,000, sells a product for $25 per unit, and has variable costs of $10 per unit. How many units must it sell to break even?
What is the simple interest earned on $15,000 invested at 4% per year for 3 years, in dollars?
$10,000 is invested at 5% annual interest, compounded annually. What is the balance after 2 years, in dollars?
An investment of $20,000 returns $26,000. What is the ROI as a percentage?
A salesperson earns a 6% commission on sales. If they sell $45,000 worth of product, what is their commission in dollars?
A restaurant bill is $230 before tax. With an 8.5% sales tax, what is the total bill in dollars?
A company has cost of goods sold of $480,000 and average inventory of $60,000. What is its inventory turnover ratio?
A $50,000 machine has a salvage value of $5,000 and a useful life of 5 years. Using straight-line depreciation, what is the annual depreciation expense in dollars?
A store buys 150 units at $12 each and sells them at $20 each, but 10 units remain unsold. What is the total profit in dollars?
A company's monthly sales grew from $45,000 to $52,200. What was the percentage increase?

A firm evaluates three projects: Project A requires $10,000 and returns $13,000; Project B requires $25,000 and returns $28,000; Project C requires $50,000 and returns $65,000. Which projects have an ROI greater than 20%? Return your answer as a JSON array of project letters.
If demand for a product is elastic and a company raises its price by 10%, explain what happens to total revenue and why.
questions.notes: Expected answer should explain that quantity demanded falls proportionally more than the price increase, so total revenue decreases.

questions.question: What is the accounting term for revenue minus the cost of goods sold?
